what_happened: Job 20261030-060751-5389 ("Check a reading's references to earlier jobs against the repo") failed in planning, before any code was written. After round 3 of 3 the critic still said the plan needed revising. The critic found the plan well grounded in the code: the functions, helpers and test seams it names all exist, and the demonstrations go through real seams. It left one major finding. Part 3 of the plan checks every job the request cites. That reverses the code's deliberate rule that jobs cited as evidence are not checked. Root-cause requests cite several rejected jobs with unlanded files, so readings that rely on none of them would be refused. The reading this job runs on would itself fail, because it names only three of the six jobs it cites. There were two minor findings (the symbol-shape rule still flags brand words, environment-variable names and local bindings; run_pin_tests.rs is not among the reading's deliverables) and one nit (paths relative to a crate go unchecked without saying so). No acceptance criteria were reported unmet and no repo checks failed. Nothing was delivered.
cause: The planner designs a new reading-refusal check from the accepted reading's wording. It does not run the check against real past request shapes, such as root-cause requests that cite many rejected jobs as evidence, and it does not test it against the job's own reading. It also does not reconcile the check with the code's existing deliberate rule that cited-as-evidence jobs are exempt. Nothing at planning time replays the proposed rule on real requests. Athena's replay runs only on built code. So the false-refusal flaw shows up only when the critic traces it by hand. The critic has a fixed three rounds and keeps no partial plan, so one late major fails the whole job and the planning spend is lost. The job's own request is a case the rule would refuse, which a self-application test would have caught.
prevention: Add a planning-stage gate for any plan that adds or changes a refusal or matching rule. The gate runs the plan's stated rule, as a small executable spec, against a stored corpus of real past requests and readings. The corpus must include the job's own request and reading and several root-cause requests that cite rejected jobs. The gate must show the rule does not refuse readings that real past work accepted. It must also show the rule is consistent with the existing code comments or rules it would reverse, such as "jobs cited as evidence are not checked". The result goes back to the planner in the early rounds, so a false-refusal defect is found before the last round. A rule may start from what the reading itself names, not from everything the request mentions.
proposed_request:
Add a check that a reading's references to earlier jobs are consistent with the repo, without refusing readings that rely on nothing from a cited job.

Outcome: when a reading names earlier jobs as things it builds on, Athena checks that the files it relies on from those jobs are present in the current repo snapshot, and refuses the reading if they are not. Jobs that the request only cites as evidence, and that the reading does not name as something it relies on, must not be checked or cause a refusal.

Acceptance:
- A reading that relies on a named earlier job whose files are not landed is refused, with a message naming the job and the missing files.
- A reading for a root-cause request that cites several rejected jobs with unlanded files, and relies on none of them, is accepted. The test uses this request's own wording and reading as one case.
- The check starts from the jobs the reading itself names as relied on. It does not start from every job id in the request text.
- Paths relative to a crate are either resolved or documented as unchecked, and a test shows which.
- The check runs inside the reading step, so a reader-level test through Athena::ask fails if it is not wired in.
- The check is replayed against stored past requests and readings, and none that were accepted before is now refused.
- A test fails without the change.

Out of scope: symbol-shape matching beyond definitions found in .rs files, and any change to dependency planning.
